PASS: PASS (round 1). Audited HEAD b7ddba8, working tree clean. Sprint 25 diff = f296262..HEAD
(8a9d263 findings, b7ddba8 code; 94127b7 is start bookkeeping).

SPRINT FILE: re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. The only change since
Master Controller's f296262 is the lifecycle-owned status: todo -> in_progress line.
No requirement amended. No A->B "arrives between versions" criterion in this sprint.

REQUIREMENTS
R1 met. docs/sprint-25-database-outage-findings.md holds five verbatim JSON
recordings (prod healthy / paused / restored, local DNS failure, local connection
refused), supabase-js 2.112.3 (matches the installed package), date 27 Sep 2026, the
measurement script source, the paused-state /api/health/db response (503, down), and
the pre-fix 404 observed live. Raw data, not a paraphrase. It also states plainly what
was NOT observed (a fetch timeout), which is the right thing to put on record. The anon
key is omitted from the curl example; I checked, and no secret is in the doc.
R2 met. One classifier, lib/supabase/availability.ts: error present, status 0, empty
code. Imported by all three call sites (reading page, horoscope action, chart save).
grep for message.includes / "fetch failed" / ENOTFOUND in app/ and lib/ returns
nothing outside tests. Fixtures are parsed out of the findings doc's own json blocks at
test time, so they cannot drift from the recording. Covered: paused (RPC and insert),
DNS, refused, 22P02, empty result, and 23502. The first test asserts the recording
count, so silently dropping a block from the doc fails the suite.
R3/R4 traced in page.tsx. Only the classifier's true verdict throws
DatabaseUnavailableError. Malformed id (22P02, status 400), missing id (null error,
empty data), and any other RPC error still fall through to the unchanged
`if (error || !data || data.length === 0) notFound()`. The thrown error's message is a
fixed string, and error.tsx reads no params and renders no error text, so nothing in
the unavailable output is derived from the id. The route has no loading.tsx and no
Suspense and no generateMetadata, so there is no early flush and no second RPC that
could 404 first. That is the static half of "the 5xx survives rendering". The real
status code is LiveQA's to prove with curl -i, as the sprint says.
R5 met. The classifier picks the message. A 23502 keeps "Save failed, try again."
(covered by a recorded fixture). The redirect still carries the date, so the cast chart
re-renders beside the error.
R6 met. app/chart/page.tsx is untouched. No database call is added to the /chart GET path.
R7 met. The action throws into the same error boundary instead of redirecting to a
page that 404s. The non-outage load failure keeps its existing redirect.
R8 met. console.error on all three unavailable paths. The reading page's notFound path
still logs nothing. The chart save's non-outage insert failure keeps the Sprint 18 R6
log it already had, which is not a 404 path.
R9 met. lib/llm/, app/api/, app/components/, ReadingPanel.tsx, app/chart/page.tsx,
layout, globals.css and package*.json are all absent from the diff. generate.test.ts
passes unmodified.

CI steps (all green locally): lint clean, typecheck clean, test 195/195 across 20
files (7 new), build compiled. Every CSS variable in unavailable.module.css already
exists. No new tokens, no new dependency.

NON-BLOCKING (low), for Dev Team or Master Controller to decide, not a condition:
app/reading/[id]/error.tsx is a route-wide error boundary, so it catches every
exception on /reading/[id], not only DatabaseUnavailableError. A render bug (say,
composeChart throwing on bad stored positions) now shows "The service behind saved
readings isn't responding." That is a false outage claim to the visitor. Its docblock
says the copy "is true for both". The heading and "try again in a few minutes" are
true for both; the service-not-responding sentence is not. Operators still see the real
error in the server log and still get a 500, so nothing is hidden from us, only
mislabelled to the visitor. The cheap fix is to drop the causal sentence and keep the
rest, which still satisfies R3. I have not reproduced this, so it is a note, not a FAIL.

No test named known-failing or pre-existing. No new Human Prerequisites: the sprint's
own pause/restore prerequisite already covers LiveQA's pass.

Handoff: Dev Team runs /sprint-dev-done 25. LiveQA owns what a static read cannot
prove: the real 5xx status via curl -i while paused, that both 404 cases still 404
while paused and after restore, and the action's error boundary in a real browser.

FAIL: FAIL (round 1). Live on production https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-09-27,
curl -i plus headless Chromium (Playwright). The Supabase project was really paused by the

b7ddba8. git diff b7ddba8 b648fe5 touches only docs/sprints/state/sprint-25.json, and the
app/ and lib/ tree hashes are identical (app 9395d930, lib 1c714266). The test is valid for
b7ddba8.

HEADLINE: all three outage paths the sprint targets behaved exactly like the pre-fix app on
a real pause. The classifier did not recognise the live paused error as unavailable on any
call site. Cause not diagnosed. I don't read code, and a direct Supabase REST probe to
capture the live paused shape was denied by the permission layer, so I dropped it. The only
live evidence of the shape is the app's own health endpoint while paused:
HTTP 503 {"status":"down","connected":false,"migrationVersion":null,"error":"Project paused.
Please unpause the project before proceeding.",...}. Dev Team should re-measure R1's
recording against a real pause. The recorded fixtures evidently do not match what
production received today.

BEFORE PAUSE (baseline), PASS:
/reading/58d6c515-7497-4fbe-bf86-e5dae76ae777 HTTP 200 (a real written reading).
/reading/abc HTTP 404. /reading/65a75e4c-29ad-4fb9-a333-85401d16444f (random uuid) HTTP 404.

WHILE PAUSED:
R3 FAIL, severity high, the sprint's core requirement. The real reading returned HTTP/2 404,
not 5xx, in 4 of 4 fetches (curl -i once, curl 3 reps) plus 1 browser load. Body text
verbatim: "404 | This page could not be found." It contains no unavailable or
not-responding wording (grep count 0). The body is byte-identical to /reading/abc's apart
from the id itself. So an outage still makes every shared link look deleted, exactly as the
Context section describes the pre-fix behaviour. The error.tsx boundary never rendered.
R4 PASS, trivially: /reading/abc and the random uuid both returned HTTP 404 "This page could
not be found.", but so did the real reading, so this proves nothing about separation.
R5 FAIL, severity high. On /chart?date=1969-07-20, "See the full reading" redirected to
/chart?date=1969-07-20&error=Save%20failed%2C%20try%20again. and the page shows verbatim
"Save failed, try again." That is the old generic message R5 replaces. The cast positions
and the date field (1969-07-20) were still shown, which is the part of R5 that holds.
R6 PASS. /chart?date=1969-07-20 returned HTTP 200 with positions rendered while paused.
R7 FAIL, severity high. On an unwritten reading (5bf3a1f5-b47f-4dfa-9a42-41f18eb24861)
loaded before the pause and held open, pressing "Write the horoscope" while paused: the
server-action POST returned 200 and the browser landed on
/reading/5bf3a1f5-...?error=Could%20not%20load%20that%20reading. rendering "404 | This page
could not be found." This is the exact pre-fix path the sprint names: redirect to a page
that reports the reading missing.
/api/health/db PASS: HTTP 503, status "down" (R9 unchanged behaviour).
R8, server-side console.error, is not observable from outside. I have no log access, so it
is untested.

AFTER RESTORE, PASS:
The real reading returned HTTP 200. /reading/abc and the random uuid both returned 404. The
held reading 5bf3a1f5 returned 200, status "NOT WRITTEN YET", so nothing was half-written by
the failed action. A full run passed: cast 1969-07-20, "See the full reading" to
/reading/7da672ea-b942-462e-8005-44028768b119, "Write the horoscope", then a reload shows
WRITTEN with the first line verbatim "Jupiter was in conjunction with Uranus in Libra when
the Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle landed on the Moon, 1969." Zero page errors.

QA1's non-blocking note (error.tsx claiming an outage for any exception) could not be
exercised. The boundary never rendered at all during the pause.

ROUND COST: the retest needs another user-scheduled pause and restore of production (Human
Prerequisite). Dev Team should confirm the classifier against a real paused response before
reshipping, so round 2 does not spend another outage finding the same thing.

PASS: LIVE-LOOP AUDIT PASS for commit eee2be7 (fix for LiveQA round 1 FAIL). eee2be7 is HEAD and the working tree is clean.
This is a record against this one commit for /sprint-reship. It is not gate 1 re-running, and it does not replace LiveQA's round-2 retest.

SPRINT FILE: re-read in full against the amended version (2ffe589). It has not changed between 2ffe589 and eee2be7. Audited against the amended R1b, R2, R4 and R8 plus the unchanged requirements.

MY OWN ROUND-1 MISS, stated so it is on record: I passed b7ddba8 without asking which way the classifier failed on a shape nobody had recorded. It failed open to "not an outage". That was the sprint's own named risk, and it is what LiveQA hit in production. This round I checked that question first.

R2 (amended), the core check: the classifier now fails closed.
isDatabaseUnavailable(operation, {error}) returns false only when error is null, or when the code is on that operation's not-an-outage list:
- lookup: exactly "22P02".
- insert: /^2[23][0-9A-Z]{3}$/, SQLSTATE class 22 or 23.
Everything else is unavailable: an empty code, a PGRST code, 42501, or any shape nobody has recorded. I checked the regex directly: 23502, 22P02, 23505 and 22001 match. 42501, PGRST002, the empty string, 4-char and 6-char codes, and 21000 do not.
The lists are per operation. A test pins that a recorded 23502 on a lookup counts as unavailable.
No message or details text is matched anywhere in app/ or lib/, and that includes "Project paused".
There is one classifier and three callers. The page and the horoscope action use "lookup", the chart save uses "insert", and each caller uses the operation that matches its call.
There is exactly one synthetic fixture (status 503, empty code). It is labelled SYNTHETIC in a comment that explains why it is allowed, and it asserts unavailable for both operations. That test fails if the default branch is ever flipped back.
All other fixtures are still parsed from the doc's recorded json blocks.

R3/R4 (amended), traced in page.tsx: after the classifier, only error null (which covers the empty result) or 22P02 can reach `if (error || !data || data.length === 0) notFound()`. Every other RPC error throws DatabaseUnavailableError into error.tsx.
During an outage the RPC never returns 22P02, so the real reading, /reading/abc and a random uuid all take the same 5xx path. That is the amended R4. The thrown error still carries a fixed message, and error.tsx is unchanged, so nothing in the unavailable output comes from the id.
The horoscope action uses the same lookup rule, so an outage at load now throws into the boundary instead of redirecting to a 404 (R7).

R5: the chart save shows the unavailable message for anything outside class 22/23. The recorded 23502 keeps "Save failed, try again." and a test covers it. The redirect still carries the date.

R8 (amended): logDatabaseUnavailable logs status, code, message, details and hint at all three unavailable call sites. A test asserts the exact logged payload against the recorded paused error. The reading route's notFound path stays silent. The chart's non-outage insert failure keeps its existing Sprint 18 log.
Limit: it copies those four named fields, so an extra field on some future error would not be logged. The amended R8 names exactly those four fields plus the status, so this meets it as written.

R1b: finding 1 is corrected to "one of at least two paused states observed". A new "Correction (LiveQA round 1)" section cites 5a874f9 and gives the ~20:53Z to 21:01:25Z window, the health route's verbatim "Project paused..." body, and what was not captured. It separates inference from observation, which is what I want in a findings doc.
The raw recordings are untouched: I diffed every json block between 2ffe589 and eee2be7 and they are byte-identical.
R1b's retest-time probe run is a round-2 action for Dev Team during the pause. It cannot be audited statically.

R6, R9: chart/page.tsx, lib/llm/, app/api/, app/components/, ReadingPanel.tsx, layout, globals.css and package*.json are all unchanged since the sprint began. generate.test.ts passes unmodified. error.tsx is unchanged since round 1.

CI: lint exit 0, typecheck exit 0, tests 197/197 across 20 files (availability has 9 tests, up from 7), build compiled.

CARRIED NOTE, still non-blocking: error.tsx's sentence "The service behind saved readings isn't responding" now covers even more cases. The amended R2 deliberately sends genuine RPC server bugs to this page too, and the sprint file accepts that cost. The sentence is still a causal claim that will sometimes be false. Master Controller accepted the 5xx; nobody has explicitly accepted that sentence. It is a one-line copy decision for Master Controller. It is not a condition.

For LiveQA round 2, which needs a paused production project: the real 5xx through curl -i for all three URLs, that the three responses are the same, vercel logs showing the full error object (this will be the first capture of the HTTP paused shape), and Dev Team's R1b probe run completing before LiveQA starts. | commit=eee2be714bd65d84f2fef4e0d05d5922d093dc36
commit=eee2be7 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for eee2be714bd65d84f2fef4e0d05d5922d093dc36 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 2), with one named limit, stated at the end. Tested live on production
https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app on 2026-09-28 against the amended sprint file (2ffe589).
Tools: curl -i, headless Chromium (Playwright), and vercel logs (the CLI is logged in as
samcollins9, so that Human Prerequisite is met).
The pause was the third, user-scheduled one. Dev Team 1's R1b probe finished before I started
(its report says the pause began about 19:27:08Z). My checks ran 19:28:09Z to 19:30Z. Restore:
/api/health/db returned ok at 19:56:46Z.

DEPLOYMENT: live is c6ce307 (reship bookkeeping). git diff eee2be7 c6ce307 touches only
docs/sprints/state/sprint-25.json. The app/ and lib/ trees are identical (app 45bd3be9,
lib 9eba49d0). So this test is valid for the reshipped eee2be7.

BEFORE PAUSE: /reading/58d6c515-7497-4fbe-bf86-e5dae76ae777 returned 200. /reading/abc
returned 404, and so did the random uuid /reading/0f34064d-4cec-4b0c-8253-5fddd6bfc36f.

WHILE PAUSED:
R3 PASS. The real reading returned HTTP 500 on all 3 curl reps, on 2 browser loads (1280px and
390px), and on 20 more reps between 19:29 and 19:30Z (20/20 were 500). The visible text,
verbatim: "TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE / This reading can't be shown right now. / The service
behind saved readings isn't responding. Try this link again in a few minutes. / CAST A NEW
CHART". The visible text never contains the id and never says not found, missing or deleted.
At 390px there is no horizontal scroll.
R4 (amended) PASS. /reading/abc and the random uuid also returned HTTP 500 on all 3 reps.
After masking the id, all three HTML bodies are byte-identical (the same md5, c0fa932d).
The id and a "This page could not be found" string do appear in the raw HTML. I located both.
The id sits only in the Next.js router segment tree (the "c":["","reading","abc"] payload).
The not-found string sits only in the framework's notFound template slot, which every page
carries, including the pre-fix 404. Neither appears in the rendered output.
R6 PASS. /chart?date=1969-07-20 returned HTTP 200 with positions rendered.
R5 PASS. "See the full reading" redirected with the new error. The page shows, verbatim:
"Readings can't be saved right now because the service is unavailable. Try again in a few
minutes." The old "Save failed, try again." is absent. The cast positions and the date field
(1969-07-20) are still shown.
R7 PASS. I held the unwritten reading a958d6d8-258b-4d50-a470-736bbdba284e open from before the
pause and pressed "Write the horoscope". The server action returned 500 and rendered the same
TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE boundary. It stayed on the reading URL with no ?error= redirect and no
404.
Health: HTTP 503, status "down". The error field reads verbatim "Project paused. Please
unpause the project before proceeding." (61 chars), consistently across 21 samples,
19:28-19:30Z.
R8 PASS, checked live with vercel logs --environment production --json --expand. Every
unavailable request logged at level error, with its call-site label and the whole object:
status, code, message, details and hint. I saw all three labels:
"ReadingPage: database unavailable", "saveReading: database unavailable" and
"generateReadingHoroscope (load): database unavailable".
Logged shape, verbatim excerpt: status: 0, code: '', message: 'TypeError: fetch failed',
details: '... Caused by: Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND rzlojpwlhbcfzpohbwso.supabase.co
(ENOTFOUND) ...', hint: ''.
After the restore, the 404 path stayed silent: /reading/abc and the uuid logged at info with an
empty message.

AFTER RESTORE, PASS: the real reading returned 200. /reading/abc and the uuid both returned
404. The held reading a958d6d8 returned 200 and still shows NOT WRITTEN YET, so the failed
action left nothing half-written.
Full run: cast 1969-07-20, then "See the full reading" to
/reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d, then "Write the horoscope". After a reload it
shows WRITTEN, beginning "Jupiter was in conjunction with Uranus on July 20, 1969." There were
zero page errors.

NAMED LIMIT (not a defect; Master Controller should weigh it). Round 1 failed on a paused
response that was NOT the DNS shape. This round, every request the app itself made while
paused, 34 logged in total, got the DNS shape: status 0 / ENOTFOUND. That includes 20
deliberate extra samples, taken while /api/health/db was reporting the HTTP "Project paused"
message the whole time. So the health route and the pages reach Supabase differently, and I
could not make the app receive a non-DNS shape. The amended classifier's default branch,
which is what fixes the round-1 failure, is therefore proven by QA1's static trace and the
synthetic unit test, not by a live observation. What I proved live: in a real outage, all
three call sites fail closed to unavailable, with the right status and copy, and log in full.
If a future pause surfaces a non-DNS shape, the full-object logging now in production will
capture it.

CARRIED from QA1, not re-litigated: error.tsx says "The service behind saved readings isn't
responding" for every exception on the route. I saw it only during real outages, where it was
true.

NOTE: sprint 25's file has changed since QA1's PASS (audited hash a28860552f21..., current f69c091896a1...). Recorded, not refused — see this function's own comment for why.
